extracted.intended_audience: film-going general audience and film critics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to understand and appreciate The Big Lebowski — why many critics missed it on first viewings and what to look for on repeat watches. Focuses on viewing strategy, character/tonal emphasis, dialogue, and expectations set by other Coen films.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Big Lebowski is a "grower" (multiple viewings needed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Big Lebowski is a "grower" — many viewers (including some critics and filmmakers) "totally didn't get it" on first viewing but appreciate it after repeated viewings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rian Johnson's admission that he 'totally didn't get it' but 'kept rewatching' is cited; anti-pattern is expecting immediate clarity and dismissing the film after one viewing. If baffled on first watch, revisit the film rather than assuming it fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot is less important than characters (character-driven film)
rubrics_metrics.description: The plot is less important than the characters; the movie functions as an exercise in character rather than a tightly plotted narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics who focused on the 'meandering plot' missed that pacing and tone are filtered through character. Evaluate how story events illuminate character rather than treating plot completeness as the primary metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enjoyment requires slipping into the rhythms of The Dude (viewpoint/tonal filter)
rubrics_metrics.description: To really enjoy the film is to 'slip into the rhythms of Jeff Bridges’ The Dude' — the story’s evolution, pacing, and tone are filtered through his lazy, weed-clouded gaze.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the film from the protagonist's perspective: consider how sequence, pacing, and ambiguity are deliberate tonal choices tied to The Dude's outlook. Anti-pattern: judging the film by conventional narrative tempo or by other characters' perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue and banter reveal deeper philosophical conflict and richness
rubrics_metrics.description: The zinging banter between characters (especially the Dude and Walter) functions as a 'battle of philosophies' and becomes richer on subsequent viewings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to dialogue, distinctive lingos, and how characters' speech patterns interact; repeated viewings reveal layers and echoes (the Dude 'absorbs and echoes' lingos). Anti-pattern: skimming dialogue or treating jokes as throwaway rather than philosophically revealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centrality of the Dude–Walter friendship (nuanced relationship)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the heart of the movie is the improbable friendship of the near-pacifist Dude and the violence-prone Walter; appreciating the film means appreciating the nuances of their friendship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate scenes for how they develop the friendship and its philosophical tensions rather than solely for plot advancement. Guidance: nuance becomes clearer after multiple viewings; anti-pattern is focusing on plot mechanics while neglecting relational dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critics' expectations based on prior Coen films can mislead (genre/expectation mismatch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics primed by the Coens' earlier, more focused works (e.g., Fargo) were disappointed by The Big Lebowski's meandering and genre-mixing; mismatched expectations can cause negative reception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating, avoid importing expectations from different works — the Coens regularly mish-mash genres and styles. Practical tip: don't introduce a Coen newcomer to a wildly different Coen film and expect the same experience (example: showing Burn After Reading after Fargo can frustrate viewers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate critical analysis may miss the film — meet the filmmakers on their level
rubrics_metrics.description: It's tough to like or fairly evaluate a movie when you're unwilling or unable to 'meet the filmmakers on their level'; immediate reviews may therefore misjudge films that require orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider reviewer stance and willingness to accept the filmmakers' approach; allow time and re-engagement before forming a final critical judgement. Anti-pattern: confidently dismissing a film for not conforming to traditional critical expectations on first exposure.
